how.title: From files to cited answers in three steps
how.subtitle: No pipelines to build. Upload, wait a few minutes, ask.

upload.title: Upload your documents
upload.body: Drag in PDF or Word files, up to 50 MB each. Every file is tracked with a clear status: Processing, Ready or Error.

index.title: They are indexed automatically
index.body: DocuMind splits each document into chunks and turns them into embeddings, so the right passages are found by meaning, not just keywords.

ask.title: Ask and verify
ask.body: Ask in natural language. The answer is generated from your documents and points to the exact source excerpt and page.

features.title: Built for answers you can trust
features.subtitle: Every design choice favors verifiable answers over confident guesses.

cited.title: Page-level citations
cited.body: Each answer links back to the source excerpt and page, so you can check it in seconds.

grounded.title: Grounded in your content
grounded.body: Answers are generated only from the documents you upload, not from the open internet.

semantic.title: Search by meaning
semantic.body: Vector search finds relevant passages even when your question uses different words than the document.

team.title: Shared team workspace
team.body: Create a company account, add your teammates and work from the same document library.

bilingual.title: English & Turkish interface
bilingual.body: Switch the whole app between English and Türkçe at any time.

selfhost.title: Open source & self-hostable
selfhost.body: MIT-licensed. Run the full stack on your own server with a single Docker Compose command.

tech.title: Under the hood
tech.body: A microservices architecture built for real workloads: uploads and embeddings scale independently, and services talk to each other over gRPC.

fileTypes.q: What file types can I upload?
fileTypes.a: PDF and Word (DOCX) files, up to 50 MB per file.

sources.q: Where do the answers come from?
sources.a: Only from the documents you uploaded. DocuMind retrieves the most relevant excerpts, generates an answer from them and references the source page.

indexing.a: Usually a few minutes, depending on document size. Each file shows its status — Processing, Ready or Error — and becomes a chat source once it is ready.

openSource.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license, and you can self-host the whole platform with Docker Compose.

stack.a: ASP.NET Core services, PostgreSQL with pgvector for similarity search, gRPC between services, MinIO for file storage, Google Gemini for generation and a Next.js web client.

cta.body: Create an account, upload a document and get a cited answer.
